 2 weather alerts in effect First Alert Weather Day: Calm conditions expected Friday 
 Lingering light to occasionally moderate intensity showers will pass across the state through Friday. By Dan Cooke , Ben Gutierrez , Jennifer Robbins , Guy Hagi and Billy V Published : Oct. 25, 2026 at 2:44 PM HST | Updated : Oct. 29, 2026 at 7:27 PM HST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - A flood advisory was in effect for the northwest Hāmākua Coast of Hawaiʻi Island until 1:15 a.m. Friday.
 At 10:13 p.m. Thursday, doppler radar showed heavy rain falling over the Waipiʻo Valley area and west of Kukuihaele at a rate of 1 to 3 inches per hour.
 Excessive rainfall was forecast to cause minor flooding on roads, in poor drainage areas and in streams. Some low-water crossings may become impassable.
 Locations expected to experience flooding include Kapaʻau, Waimanu Valley, Waipiʻo Valley, Pololū Valley, Kukuihaele, Kamuela, Hālaʻula and Hāwī.
 Your HNN First Alert Weather Team declared Thursday a First Alert Weather Day for Maui County and Hawaii Island. Both counties were under various alerts throughout most of the day.

 Improvement expected Friday
 Some localized heavy rain will still be possible into Friday for areas of windward East Maui and windward Hawaii Island. More stable conditions should prevail by Friday afternoon statewide.
 Weather for Halloween trick-or-treating could still be wet, with scattered showers mainly for windward and mauka areas for the eastern end of the state.
 Your First Alert Weather Team will closely monitor conditions and First Alert you to any changes.
 More typical trade winds briefly return but at times wet trades passing over the state (hnn) Copyright 2026 Hawaii News Now. All rights reserved.
